title: ExecVLA: Following Fine-Grained Execution Constraints in Vision-Language-Action Models with Bi-Level Action Representation
abstract: arXiv:2603.17524v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study fine-grained execution-constraint following in vision-language-action (VLA) models. Given an invariant task goal, the policy must follow instruction-specified execution constraints, including interaction targets, motion patterns, spatial relations, and terminal configurations. This setting exposes a limitation of goal-oriented VLAs: trajectories that complete the same task are not interchangeable when the instruction specifies how the task must be executed. We propose ExecVLA, a framework that separates a goal-oriented component from an execution-specific component through a bi-level action representation and supervised bi-level reasoning tokens. We further introduce explicit goal-invariance and execution-predictability objectives so that the goal-level representation remains stable across executions of the same goal, while the execution-level representation retains the constraints that distinguish those executions. translated_title: ExecVLA：通过双层动作表示使视觉-语言-动作模型遵循细粒度执行约束
translated_abstract: 我们研究了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型中对细粒度执行约束的遵循问题。在任务目标保持不变的情况下，策略必须遵循指令所指定的执行约束，包括交互目标、运动模式、空间关系和终端配置。这一设定揭示了面向目标的VLA模型的一个局限性：当指令规定了任务的执行方式时，完成同一任务的不同轨迹是不可互换的。我们提出了ExecVLA，这是一个通过双层动作表示和有监督的双层推理标记，将面向目标的组件与执行特定的组件分离开来的框架。我们进一步引入了显式的目标不变性和执行可预测性目标，使得目标级表示在同一目标的多次执行中保持稳定，而执行级表示则保留了区分这些不同执行的约束信息。
tldr: 提出ExecVLA框架，通过双层动作表示将目标导向组件与执行特定组件解耦，使VLA模型能够遵循指令指定的细粒度执行约束。
en_tdlr: ExecVLA is proposed as a framework that decouples goal-oriented components from execution-specific components via bi-level action representation, enabling VLA models to follow fine-grained instruction-specified execution constraints.
